https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/08/arge.text: The Argentine government announced on Monday that it will file a criminal complaint against several subsidiaries of the Israeli oil company Navitas for operating without authorisation in the Malvinas (Falkland Islands), which are administered by the United Kingdom but whose sovereignty is claimed by Argentina.The decision triggered an immediate reaction in Israel. The Minister for National Security, Itamar Ben Gvir, called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereignty over the Malvinas and to impose sanctions on the United Kingdom "for as long as the occupation continues", accusing London of seizing Argentine territory and oil resources.According to the Argentine presidency, the complaint will target Navitas Petroleum Development & Production Ltd, Navitas Petroleum Atlantic United, Navitas Petroleum LP, JHI Associates Inc and Eco Atlantic Oil & Gas Ltd, as well as their executives and representatives.Argentina maintains that these companies "allegedly hold licences granted by the illegitimate government of the United Kingdom" to explore and exploit hydrocarbons in the North Malvinas Basin, in violation of Argentine law. The case also targets directors, managers, statutory auditors and any representatives who have taken part in the project.This is not the first time Buenos Aires has taken action over oil activity in the area. Argentina had already declared these operations illegal in 2012 and filed a similar complaint in 2015. In 2022 it sanctioned Navitas directly and, in December 2025, Javier Milei's government formally rejected investors' announcement they will pour €1.808 billion into the project to start production.Sea Lion, the oilfield at the heart of the disputeNavitas operates and controls 65% of the Sea Lion project, located around 220 kilometres north of the Falkland Islands, in waters disputed by Argentina and the United Kingdom. Its partner is the British company Rockhopper, which owns the remaining 35%. The project is in the development phase and is expected to start pumping crude oil in March 2028.The two companies had already responded to the measures announced by Argentina before the criminal complaint was submitted. Following Milei's speech last Thursday, they issued a joint statement insisting that they operate under licences "legally granted" by the islands' government and with "the full and ongoing support" of the United Kingdom.The companies stressed that they do not expect the Argentine measures to delay the Sea Lion project timeline. Rockhopper's shares fell by more than 6% on the London Stock Exchange after the announcement.Ben Gvir urges Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereigntyThe complaint against the subsidiaries of an Israeli oil company comes amid rising diplomatic tension between Israel and the United Kingdom. Ben Gvir called on Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereignty over the territory and to adopt sanctions against London "for as long as the occupation continues".The Israeli minister accused the United Kingdom of seizing territory and oil resources that, he argued, belong to the Argentine people. Hours earlier, Israel's Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, had called for the expulsion of the British ambassador to Israel.The remarks come amid widening rifts between London and Tel Aviv over British policy towards Palestine. For the moment, Ben Gvir's words do not amount to a change in Israel's official position on the islands' sovereignty.Milei steps up his offensivePresident Javier Milei announced on Thursday that he intends to toughen sanctions on oil companies operating in the Falkland Islands under licences issued by the British territory. He also said he would send a bill to Congress that would extend sanctions to the suppliers of these companies and bar offenders from contracting with the Argentine state.That same day he confirmed that he will revive plans to build a naval base in Ushuaia, around 700 kilometres from the islands. On Monday, Milei instructed Economy Minister Luis Caputo to give the project priority in the 2027 budget, which the government will send to Congress this month."These measures are part of a comprehensive policy aimed at strengthening the Argentine state's ability to defend its territory, protect its natural resources and safeguard its strategic interests," the government said in a statement.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/thousands.text: Paul Withers Updated Sat, October 10, 2026 at 10:40 AM UTC 130 Tunnels under the Lithuanian border are the new routes for migrants trying to reach Western Europe (Image: State Border Guard Services) Thousands of migrants are being smuggled through secret tunnels amid fears they could be heading towards the UK, it has been claimed. A Great Escape-style underground passage, dug by 'human mole' smugglers from Belarus to Luthuania, has reportedly been discovered beneath the European Union's border. Eighteen migrants were recently caputed on video by The Sun crawling through the 50ft-long tunnel, before clambering from an exit hole and dashing into thick forest. The secret passageway was reportedly discovered in remote forest near Kabeliai in southern Lithuania amid fears this and other tunnels are being used by migrants trying to reach the UK and large parts of Western Europe. In 2026, Lithuania has found 12 secret tunnels, while border guards in nearby Latvia have discovered two more. The tunnels are destroyed by the Baltic countries as soon as they are uncovered. Lithuania's Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas said: "The threat of irregular migration is growing. Tunnels dug under the state border are becoming an unlawful alternative for entering Lithuania illegally." Recently, border officers found two tunnels - one as long as 130ft - which smugglers had seemingly burrowed under a border fence, according to The Sun. In August, 28 migrants were detained by Latvian border guards after the group had crawled through an underground passage from Belarus. This year alone, nearly 12,000 migrants have already seen their attempts to cross the Baltic nation's border fence scuppered. Latvian officials seem in little doubt Belarus - a staunch ally of Vladimr Putin - is playing a large role in the influx of migrants. Several illicit tunnels under the Lithuanian border have been discovered (Image: State Border Guard Services) Captain Vladimirs Sersts from Latvia's State Border Guard said: "When you see a group of migrants freely walking along the fence on the Belarusian side, this is your answer. This is a restricted area." Latvia and Lithuania have become close allies of Ukraine in the four-and-a-half years since the invasion into the eastern country by Putin's forces. Margarita Seselgyte, Director of the Institute of International Relations and Political Science at Vilnius University, believes the tunnels are "a hybrid attack to cause anxiety in our society". She added: "The main goal is probably to weaken support for Ukraine and disrupt European unity." Since the infamous border crisis in 2021, Lithuania has managed to stop more than 26,000 migrants from entering the country from Belarus. In 2026 alone, almost 1,700 migrants have been prevented from crossing. Yet, this reportedly doesn't seem to be deterring the tunnellers. In July, it was revealed work by smugglers on an unfinished 36ft-long underground shaft were compromised by a Lithuanian border patrol. Alp Mehmet, Chairman of Migration Watch UK, told me: "It's not unusual for some EU countries to do migrant push backs. "I find it very difficult to understand why France in particular doesn't take illegal migrants back from Britain. It beggars belief that Britain is paying the French through the nose to stop migrants for nothing in return." Downing Street has insisted English Channel migrant crossings are 'down significantly' (Image: Getty) Earlier this week, two men have died attempting a small boat crossing of the English Channel, with the French authorities urging migrants not to risk the journey. They said the men, one thought to be in his 30s and the other in his 40s, died after leaving the coast at Berck on Sunday night. Three other people among the 90 on board the vessel also needed treatment after prolonged contact with fuel in the boat, the local maritime prefecture said. According to a translation of the prefecture's statement, a separate incident last Sunday morning saw a boat containing around 80 migrants run aground at Camiers. Most of the migrants waded back to the beach but 11 people were rescued suffering from hypothermia. The Maritime Prefecture of the English Channel and the North Sea warned that the "flimsy inflatable boats used for such crossings are unsuitable and particularly vulnerable" to the conditions in the busy sea lanes between France and the UK. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's official spokesman recently said: "Crossings are down significantly - 44% on last year - and this summer saw the lowest number of small boat arrivals in six years. We've removed more than 80,000 people with no right to be here since the election, an increase of 52%."
